Amgen vs. Vertex Pharmaceuticals: Which Healthcare Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
sum: Инвесторы, ищущие стабильности в секторе здравоохранения, часто сравнивают Amgen (AMGN -0,30%) и Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX -0,74%). Выбор между этими двумя лидерами отрасли требует баланса между диверсифицированным доходом и быстрорастущей специализацией.

Amgen предлагает широкий спектр продуктов для лечения онкологии и редких заболеваний, обеспечивая устойчивую бизнес-модель. Vertex Pharmaceuticals специализируется на преобразующих методах лечения конкретных генетических заболеваний, приносящих высокую прибыль. Обе компании представляют разные способы использования постоянных инноваций в медицинской сфере.

Amgen разрабатывает и производит лекарства для лечения широкого спектра серьезных заболеваний — от воспалений до онкологии. Она продает в основном трем крупным дистрибьюторам: McKesson Corp. (MCK +2,39%), Cencora Inc. (COR +2,96%) и Cardinal Health (CAH +1,06%), на которые пришлось почти 77% ее доходов в 2025 году. Подобная концентрация клиентов добавляет дополнительный уровень риска для бизнеса, хотя и упрощает логистику глобальной дистрибьюторской сети.

За 12 месяцев, закончившихся 30 сентября 2026 года, выручка достигла примерно $38,9 млрд, что представляет собой рост примерно на 8,3% по сравнению с предыдущим периодом. За тот же период компания получила чистую прибыль в размере почти $9,4 млрд. Этот рост отражает продолжающееся расширение основного портфеля компании и ее стратегический выход на новые рынки, такие как Китай и Япония.

По состоянию на декабрь 2025 года соотношение долга к собственному капиталу составляло примерно 6,3x. Этот коэффициент измеряет левередж путем сравнения общего долга с акционерным капиталом, показывая, что Amgen использует значительный заемный капитал для финансирования своей деятельности. Текущий коэффициент, который измеряет способность платить по краткосрочным обязательствам, был близок к 1,1x, а свободный денежный поток за финансовый год, закончившийся 31 декабря 2025 года, достиг примерно $8,1 млрд.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals является лидером среди акций биотехнологических компаний, известных своим доминированием в сфере лечения муковисцидоза. Компания успешно расширила сферу своей деятельности, включив в нее серповидноклеточную анемию, благодаря совместной разработке препарата Casgevy с CRISPR Therapeutics (CRSP -0,89%). Компания также использует соглашения об аутлицензии для других кандидатов с такими партнерами, как Zai Lab (ZLAB -5,53%), чтобы максимизировать охват своей интеллектуальной собственности.

Vertex Pharma stock rises as FDA decision nears
sum: Vertex Pharmaceuticals is approaching a key regulatory date after reporting stronger third-quarter sales and raising its full-year outlook. The company said on November 2 that revenue for the quarter ended September 30 increased 12 percent year over year to 3.44 billion US dollars, according to its third-quarter financial release.

Cystic fibrosis products remained the main revenue source, generating 3.27 billion US dollars in the quarter. Newer products also contributed, with CASGEVY revenue of 99.2 million US dollars, JOURNAVX revenue of 58.3 million US dollars and PALSONIFY revenue of 10.1 million US dollars.

Vertex lifted its 2026 total revenue guidance to 13.15 billion to 13.25 billion US dollars from 13.1 billion to 13.2 billion previously. The outlook includes at least 500 million US dollars from CASGEVY and JOURNAVX combined and 40 million to 50 million US dollars from PALSONIFY.

Reported earnings faced pressure from the Crinetics Pharmaceuticals acquisition and broader commercial investment. GAAP net income fell to 653.6 million US dollars from 1.08 billion US dollars a year earlier, while non-GAAP net income was 1.21 billion US dollars compared with 1.24 billion US dollars.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has assigned November 30 as the PDUFA target action date for povetacicept in IgA nephropathy. Vertex's application is under priority review and is supported by interim Phase 3 RAINIER results. If approved, povetacicept would become the company's first commercialized nephrology therapy.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals stock traded at 491.55 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:15 CET on Thursday, November 12, 2026. That was 1.30 percent above the 485.25-euro quote cited in the previous report published on November 11; this separate report-to-report comparison is not a Xetra session comparison.

For investors, the raised outlook offers evidence of expanding commercial contributions, while the upcoming FDA decision represents a binary regulatory catalyst. The company is also increasing spending to support the renal franchise, the Crinetics integration and the JOURNAVX launch.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated (VRTX) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
sum: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated operates as a biotechnology company in the United States, Europe, and internationally. The company offers transformative medicines for people with serious diseases with a focus on specialty markets, such as cystic fibrosis (CF), sickle cell disease (SCD), transfusion dependent beta thalassemia (TDT), and acute pain. It markets TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO for people with CF with at least one F508del mutation for 2 years of age and older; ALYFTREK for the treatment for people with CF 6 years of age and older; SYMDEKO/SYMKEVI for treatment of patients with CF 6 years of age and older; ORKAMBI for CF patients 1 year or older; and KALYDECO for the treatment of patients with 1 month or older who have CF with ivacaftor. The company also develops CASGEVY for the treatment of SCD and TDT; JOURNAVX for the treatment of acute pain in adults; VX-522, a CFTR mRNA therapeutic designed to treat the underlying cause of CF, which is in Phase 1/2 clinical trial; inaxaplin for the treatment of APOL1-mediated kidney disease, which is in single Phase 2 trial; VX-264 for treating Type 1 Diabetes; VX-670 for the treatment of myotonic dystrophy type 1; and VX-407, a small molecule corrector for the treatment of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. In addition, the company also operates as a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, that focuses on the discovery, development, and commercialization of novel therapeutics for rare endocrine diseases and endocrine-related tumors. The company sells its products primarily to specialty pharmacy and distributors, wholesalers, retail pharmacies, hospitals, and clinics. Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated has a strategic collaboration with AbCellera Biologics Inc. to research, develop, manufacture, and commercialize multispecific T-cell engagers (TCEs) for autoimmune diseases and other conditions. Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated was founded in 1989 and is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts.

The Vertex selection covers commercial-scale production of povetacicept, a programme Evotec is pursuing in tandem with the US Department of Defense. Alongside that win, the company reported advances across its collaborations and development programmes.

Net sales in the D&PD base core business ran 24% above the prior-year comparative period, the company said.

sum: Investors choosing between Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY -1.57%) and Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX +0.85%) must decide between a steady value play and a high-growth innovator as they look toward 2027.

Bristol Myers Squibb operates as a diversified drug manufacturer with a vast global infrastructure and several blockbuster treatments. Vertex Pharmaceuticals acts as a focused biotechnology leader, using advanced science to create near-monopolies in specific disease niches. This comparison explores their financial health and risk profiles to determine which fits your investment strategy.

Bristol Myers Squibb develops and delivers medicines for serious conditions, specifically in the fields of oncology, hematology, and neuroscience. The company sells its products mainly to wholesalers, distributors, and specialty pharmacies, while maintaining key alliances with partners like BioNTech (BNTX +1.92%) for global strategic collaborations. It also holds an agreement with the U.S. government to provide certain medications, such as Eliquis, to the Medicaid program.

In FY 2025, revenue reached around $48.2 billion, reflecting a slight decline of roughly 0.2% compared to the previous year. Despite this flat top-line growth, the company reported a net income of about $7.1 billion for the period. This represents a significant recovery from the prior year and resulted in a net margin, which measures how much profit is kept from every dollar of sales, of approximately 14.6%.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company carries a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 2.6x, indicating that its total liabilities are 2.6 times the value of its shareholder equity. Its current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term bills with short-term assets, is approximately 1.3x. For the fiscal year, free cash flow reached about $12.8 billion, which is the cash remaining after the company pays for its operating activities and capital expenditures.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals focuses on transformative medicines for specialty markets, including cystic fibrosis and sickle cell disease. By targeting biotech stocks that dominate specific therapeutic areas, investors can often find companies with high pricing power.

The next major event is the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's target action date of November 30 for povetacicept in IgA nephropathy. Vertex said the application is under priority review and that approval would make the drug its first commercialized nephrology therapy. sum: Vertex Pharmaceuticals VRTX reported adjusted earnings of $4.76 per share for the third of 2026, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.92. Earnings declined 0.8% year over year as higher product revenues were offset by increased operating expenses, higher interest costs and lower interest income.

Total revenues rose 12% year over year, primarily driven by higher sales of cystic fibrosis (CF) drugs Trikafta/Kaftrio and Alyftrek, as well as meaningful contributions from other new products, Journavx and Casgevy. The company also benefited from the addition of Palsonify following its acquisition of Crinetics Pharmaceuticals in September 2026.

Alyftrek, a next-in-class triple combination regimen for CF, generated sales of $705.8 million in the third quarter, up 23% sequentially, reflecting continued uptake across multiple geographies. During the quarter, Vertex secured reimbursement for Alyftrek in seven additional countries, bringing the total to 32.
Revenues from other CF products decreased 6.3% year over year to $130.5 million.

Revenues from Vertex and partner CRISPR Therapeutics’ CRSP gene therapy, Casgevy, were $99.2 million in the third quarter, up approximately 30% sequentially and 487% year over year. Higher sales reflected increasing patient infusions.

The company announced the Phase 3 RAINIER findings on October 23, when the results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine and presented at the American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week. The Vertex Pharmaceuticals release said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has set November 30, 2026, as the PDUFA target action date for potential accelerated approval.

Vertex said the trial met its primary endpoint and both secondary endpoints. In the prespecified Week 36 interim analysis, povetacicept reduced proteinuria by 52.0 percent from baseline, producing a statistically significant 49.8 percent reduction versus placebo. The treatment is an engineered fusion protein designed to inhibit the BAFF and APRIL cytokines, which are involved in B-cell activity and the disease process of IgA nephropathy.

The results also showed a clinically relevant response on a kidney-related measure. A 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio below 0.5 grams per gram was reached by 42.2 percent of participants receiving povetacicept, compared with 6.2 percent in the placebo group. Vertex said the finding was observed on top of optimized supportive care, including sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use in 65.8 percent of participants.

Both secondary endpoints also favored povetacicept. Serum galactose-deficient IgA1 fell 77.4 percent from baseline in the treatment group, while the placebo group recorded a 9.1 percent increase. Among participants with blood in the urine at baseline, hematuria resolved in 85.1 percent of those receiving povetacicept versus 23.4 percent on placebo.

The safety profile was generally favorable in the interim assessment. Most adverse events were mild to moderate, and Vertex reported no serious adverse events related to povetacicept and no deaths in the trial. Injection-site reactions occurred in 14.5 percent of treated participants and 2.2 percent of those receiving placebo, while upper respiratory tract infections occurred in 18.3 percent and 11.4 percent, respectively.

sum: Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) shares surged to an all-time high Monday after Sionna Therapeutics (SION) reported a stunning clinical failure for its experimental cystic fibrosis drug, effectively neutralizing one of the most closely watched threats to Vertex's dominant respiratory franchise.

The stock climbed roughly 6% to 7% in the session, pushing past $526, as investors recalibrated the competitive landscape. The catalyst was Sionna's announcement that its Phase 2a PreciSION CF trial for SION-719, designed as an add-on to Vertex's blockbuster Trikafta, missed its key efficacy endpoint by a wide margin. Sionna shares, meanwhile, collapsed more than 90% to a record low.

BMO Capital analyst Evan David Seigerman framed the outcome bluntly: "We view this clinical development as a strong positive for VRTX; expect shares strength on a major overhang removed." The failure reinforces the durability of Vertex's cystic fibrosis franchise, which generated roughly $3.33 billion in second-quarter revenue, up 12% from a year earlier. Management recently raised its full-year revenue guidance to a range of $13.1 billion to $13.2 billion.

The trial evaluated SION-719 at 30 milligrams twice daily when added to Trikafta in adults with cystic fibrosis who were homozygous for the F508del mutation. The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study enrolled 15 participants who had been stable on physician-prescribed Trikafta for at least three months before screening. After a 14-day Trikafta run-in, participants received 14 days of SION-719 plus Trikafta and 14 days of placebo plus Trikafta in randomized order, separated by a 28-day washout period.

Sionna had powered the study to detect a sweat chloride improvement of at least 10 mmol/L, a threshold management considered potentially clinically meaningful. The actual result was a placebo-adjusted change of negative 1 mmol/L, with a p-value of 0.7. Sweat chloride is a key biomarker of CFTR function, the defective protein that causes cystic fibrosis.
"We are deeply disappointed to announce that PreciSION CF Phase 2a trial did not meet its key activity endpoint," Sionna President and Chief Executive Officer Mike Cloonan said.

Vertex's CF franchise remains strong as demand for its CF therapies continues to grow, as the company expands access globally and wins approvals in younger patient populations. Meanwhile, Vertex does not face any near-term headwinds from LOE or increased competition for its CF therapies.

Its CF products generated revenues of $2.92 billion in the first quarter of 2026, up 6.2% year over year, driven by Trikafta/Kaftrio as well as increasing contribution from Alyftrek, a next-in-class triple combination regimen and Vertex's fifth and newest CF medicine.

Alphabet stock is down but analysts are not giving up on it
sum: Alphabet shares dropped 1.44% today to $286.70, extending a stretch of short and medium-term weakness even as analysts continued to build a case for the stock as one of the most complete AI investments available in the market. The decline comes as investors broadly reassess how much value is actually being created by the wave of AI infrastructure spending that has reshaped the technology sector over the past two years.

The core argument being made by several market commentators centers on what Alphabet brings together that no single competitor fully replicates. The combination of its Gemini foundational large language models, its in-house tensor processing units, its Google Cloud platform, its dominance in Search, and assets including subsea cable networks and cybersecurity firm Wiz represents a breadth of AI-linked infrastructure that analysts describe as unmatched.

The TPU argument is particularly central to the bull case. Alphabet has been developing its custom AI chips for more than a decade, refining them across multiple generations and using them internally to train its own models. That lead time matters because building competitive custom silicon is slow and expensive. Other companies are catching up, but Alphabet’s incumbency in this area is treated as a structural advantage that is difficult to replicate quickly. Notably, Meta Platforms is using Alphabet’s TPUs for some AI workloads despite developing its own custom accelerators, which has been cited as an indication of their quality.

One line of current market discussion holds that Alphabet’s stock could climb roughly 35% by the end of 2026, which would push its market capitalization toward $5 trillion. The catalyst for that projection is AI-driven acceleration across Cloud and Search, two segments that together generate the overwhelming majority of the company’s revenue.

Google Cloud delivered particularly notable results in the fourth quarter, with revenue growing 48% year over year. That growth reflected demand for both AI infrastructure, including GPU and TPU access for developers building and training large language models, and AI services built on top of that infrastructure.

2 Biotech Giants to Buy in 2026
sum: Biotech stocks may offer your portfolio an element of growth, and that's because these companies are sharply focused on innovation. They set out to tackle some of the most challenging diseases, and as they progress toward the finish line, their stock prices might take off. And once they actually reach their goals and commercialize a product or products, these players should continue to offer you growth, and at the same time, an element of safety -- the idea here is patients need their medications, so revenue may achieve a certain stability.
With this in mind, let's check out two biotech giants that have proven themselves with solid pipelines and a number of products on the market. They make great additions to any portfolio in 2026.

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN +1.73%) has two big sources of growth right now: Dupixent, a drug that treats inflammatory conditions from eczema to asthma, and Eylea HD, a drug for retinal disease. In the recent quarter, global sales of the former rose 34% and U.S. sales of the latter jumped 66%. The biotech company is also generating double-digit growth from cancer immunotherapy Libtayo. These and other products have helped Regeneron increase earnings over time.

On top of this, Regeneron has a rich pipeline, including many late-stage programs in areas spanning hematology, immunology, and rare disease. This should fuel new stages of growth down the road -- even if only a handful make it to commercialization.
All of this makes Regeneron look like a very reasonable buy at 17x forward earnings estimates, down from past levels that surpassed 25x projected earnings.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX +0.69%) is the leading player in the field of cystic fibrosis (CF) treatment. The company sells blockbuster drugs known as CFTR modulators, and they're designed to fix a faulty protein that leads to disease symptoms. Today, Vertex's drugs may treat 90% of the CF patient population, and the company is working on a candidate to address those who can't benefit from its current products.
Importantly, Vertex has strong intellectual property that should protect its CF leadership into the later part of the next decade.

sum: Vertex Pharmaceuticals stock (VRTX) trades at $474.27 after a 2.4% pullback, yet 77,000 CF patients on therapy and $12.3 billion in cash signal a company running far ahead of its stock price.

Multiple Vertex executives, including EVP and Chief Commercial Officer Duncan McKechnie and Chief Legal Officer Jonathan Biller, disposed of common shares between February 18 and March 2, while the stock sits 8.8% below its 52-week high of $519.68.

Vertex posted $12 billion in full-year 2025 revenue, grew Q4 earnings 24% year-over-year to $1.3 billion, and guided 2026 revenue to $12.95 billion to $13.1 billion, with non-CF products alone targeting $500 million or more.

Meanwhile, the pending pove IgAN interim analysis from the RAINIER trial, confirmed for H1 2026, carried additional weight after Reshma Kewalramani, CEO, stated on the Q4 earnings call that “pove is administered as a once-monthly small volume subcutaneous dose delivered via an auto-injector,” a profile nephrologists have already flagged as their preferred administration format across 74 payer engagements covering 210 million lives.

With TRIKAFTA patents intact until 2037, ALYFTREK protected beyond that, and four commercial verticals converging alongside five pivotal-stage programs, Vertex enters a multi-year window where renal alone, anchored by pove across IgAN, membranous nephropathy, and myasthenia gravis, could rival the scale of its CF franchise.

Vertex’s confirmed H1 pove IgAN interim readout from the RAINIER trial directly determines whether management completes its BLA submission and unlocks a renal franchise analysts expect to rival CF in scale.

The fundamental case holds firm: revenue grows from $12 billion in 2025 to an estimated $13 billion in 2026, while normalized EPS climbs from $18.40 to $19.17, sustaining a business that has compounded revenue at 14.1% annually over five years.

sum: Vertex executives warned that Casgevy, its curative treatment for sickle cell disease, would be slow to reach patients. But few expected it to be this slow.

More than two years after its approval, only about 60 patients across the U.S., Middle East, and Europe have been treated with the gene-editing therapy. Specialists at four sickle centers told STAT they’ve been surprised by one of the key stumbling blocks to faster rollout: They can’t collect enough cells to create the treatment.
The problem comes at a crucial time for Vertex, which is trying to establish Casgevy even as it fights off rival therapies and braces for a major competitor next year.
